The '''Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry''' is a rivalry between London-based professional [[association football]] clubs [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal Football Club]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]]. Arsenal play their home games at the [[Emirates Stadium]], while Chelsea play their home games at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]].

Overall, Arsenal have won more games in the rivalry's history, having won 88 times to Chelsea's 66, with 62 draws as of match played on 6 September 2026.<ref name="soccerbaseh2h2">{{cite web|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/teams/team.sd?team_id=142&team2_id=536&teamTabs=h2h |title=Arsenal vs. Chelsea |work=Soccerbase|access-date=6 September 2026}}</ref> Arsenal's record win was a 5–0 victory in a [[Premier League]] match at Emirates Stadium on 23 April 2024, and Chelsea's record win was a 6–0 victory at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League on 22 March 2014. [[Didier Drogba]] holds the mark for the most derby goals with 13 in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Drog the Arsenal hunter |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2020/05/20/drog-the-arsenal-hunter |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |access-date=23 October 2020 |date=20 May 2020}}</ref>

The clubs have contested five major finals: the [[2002 FA Cup final]], which Arsenal won 2–0, the [[2007 Football League Cup final|2007 League Cup final]], which Chelsea won 2–1, the [[2017 FA Cup final]], which Arsenal won 2–1, the [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|2019 Europa League final]], which Chelsea won 4–1, and the [[2020 FA Cup final]], which Arsenal won 2–1.

==Background==
While they have never considered each other primary rivals, as two of the biggest and most successful clubs in London there has always been strong needle between the fans dating back to the 1930s. Matches between them would often attract large attendances.

The Arsenal and Chelsea rivalry has been more recently considered an important derby, after Chelsea's rise to the top class of the [[Premier League]] in the 2000s, when the two started to compete consistently for the [[English football champions|Premier League title]].

According to an internet survey of fans in December 2003, the Arsenal fans who responded to the survey said that they considered Chelsea as their third rival, after [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|Manchester United]] and [[North London Derby|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref name="census">{{cite web|url=http://www.footballfanscensus.com/issueresults/Club_Rivalries_Uncovered_Results.pdf |title=Rivalry Uncovered! |publisher=The Football Fans Census |page=3 |date=December 2003 |access-date=1 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080227004632/http://www.footballfanscensus.com/issueresults/Club_Rivalries_Uncovered_Results.pdf |archive-date=27 February 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Those Chelsea fans who responded to the survey said that they considered Arsenal as their main rival, however Tottenham and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] are their more traditional rivals.<ref name="census"/>

In a 2008 survey by the Football Fans Census, Arsenal fans named Chelsea as the club they disliked the most, ahead of their traditional rivals Tottenham. Chelsea fans have named Arsenal as their second-most disliked club, behind [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.footballfanscensus.com/londonfootballreport08.pdf |title=London Football Report |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301000000/http://www.footballfanscensus.com/londonfootballreport08.pdf |archive-date=1 March 2014 |access-date=9 February 2013 }}</ref> A 2014 [[Bleacher Report]] article ranks Arsenal as Chelsea's second-most hated rival.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chelsea FC: Ranking the Blues' 5 Most Hated Rivals|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1048256-chelsea-fc-ranking-the-blues-5-most-hated-rivals|website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

==History==
The first league meeting between the two teams took place on 9 November 1907 at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]]. This was the first [[Football League First Division]] game played between two London clubs and drew a crowd of 65,000.<ref name="1stmatch">{{cite web|url=http://www.11v11.com/matches/chelsea-v-woolwich-arsenal-09-november-1907-57449/|title=Chelsea v Woolwich Arsenal, 09 November 1907|website=11v11.com|access-date=9 February 2017}}</ref> A match between the clubs at Stamford Bridge in 1935 drew a crowd of 82,905,<ref name="attendances">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/chelsea-article/article/1336457/title/attendances|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|title=Attendances|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140626074307/http://www.chelseafc.com/chelsea-article/article/1336457/title/attendances|archive-date=26 June 2014|access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref> the second highest recorded attendance for an English league match.<ref>{{cite web |title=Top 30 record home attendances in English football history, including Aston Villa, Chelsea, Manchester City and Newcastle |url=https://talksport.com/football/354931/record-attendances-football-aston-villa-chelsea-newcastle-city/ |website=[[Talksport]]|access-date=24 January 2021 |date=17 November 2018}}</ref> They met in two close contested [[FA Cup]] semi-finals in the 1950s, with Arsenal winning both times. In the 1960s Chelsea dominated the tie with 14 wins, two draws and just two losses during the decade.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120526074859/http://review.chelseafc.com/page/LatestNews/0%2C%2C10268~1471656%2C00.html Derby Debate – Past and Present]. review.chelseafc.com (29 November 2008). Retrieved on 9 February 2013.</ref>

The two teams have met in the quarter-finals of the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League]], with Chelsea winning [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Chelsea v Arsenal|3–2]] on aggregate to go through to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal 1–2 Chelsea |website=BBC Sport|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/champions_league/3593083.stm |access-date=30 May 2019 |date=6 April 2004}}</ref>

In 2006, the transfer of [[Ashley Cole]] from Arsenal to Chelsea further stoked the rivalry, as Cole had been caught meeting Chelsea officials months before.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article632948.ece | work=The Times | location=London | title = The Ashley Cole transfer saga | date = 8 September 2006 | access-date = 25 April 2010 }}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

The [[2007 Football League Cup final]] was one of the most noted incidents. The game was marred by a fracas involving [[Frank Lampard]], [[Cesc Fàbregas]] and others that resulted in yellow cards for the two and three other players sent off, the dismissal of [[Emmanuel Adebayor]] and incidents of Chelsea fans throwing celery at Arsenal players.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bandini |first1=Nicky |title=Football: Chelsea ban supporters from bringing celery into their Stamford Bridge stadium |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/mar/16/newsstory.sport11 |website=The Guardian |access-date=29 December 2019 |date=16 March 2007}}</ref> This led the media to dub it the "Snarling Cup final".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Krishnan |first1=Joe |title=From Kanu's cracker to the 'Snarling Cup' - the top five Arsenal v |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/from-kanus-cracker-to-the-snarling-cup-the-top-five-arsenal-v-chelsea-matches-9016060.html |website=Evening Standard |access-date=23 May 2019 |date=23 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Duleep Allirajah |title=The 'Snarling' Cup: when in doubt, start a fight |url=https://www.spiked-online.com/2007/03/01/the-snarling-cup-when-in-doubt-start-a-fight/ |website=spiked-online.com |access-date=23 May 2019 |date=1 March 2007}}</ref> The match ended in a 2–1 victory for Chelsea.

On 27 December 2010, Chelsea came into the [[Emirates Stadium|Emirates]] having beaten Arsenal five times in a row by a goal difference of 13–2, only for Arsenal to win the match 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9309539.stm|title=Arsenal 3–1 Chelsea|website=BBC Sport|date=27 December 2010|first=Phil|last=McNulty}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/dec/27/arsenal-chelsea-premier-league-match-report|title=Ruthless Arsenal come of age to turn Chelsea's slump into a crisis|website=The Guardian|date=27 December 2010|first=Kevin|last=McCarra}}</ref>

On 29 October 2011, Arsenal won 5–3 at Stamford Bridge after coming from behind twice, with [[Robin van Persie]] scoring two late goals and completing his [[hat-trick]]. It is widely regarded as one of the most memorable and best games between the two sides.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea vs Arsenal: 7 Classic Clashes Between London's Millennial Rivals |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/6597394-chelsea-vs-arsenal-7-classic-clashes-between-london-s-millennial-rivals |website=90min.com |access-date=23 October 2020 |date=21 April 2020 |archive-date=27 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027023506/https://www.90min.com/posts/6597394-chelsea-vs-arsenal-7-classic-clashes-between-london-s-millennial-rivals |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Mattias Karen |author2=Liam Twomey |title=Arsenal vs. Chelsea: 10 memorable games |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/barclays-premier-league/23/blog/post/2791527/arsenal-vs-chelsea-10-memorable-games |website=ESPN |access-date=23 October 2020 |date=23 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Bower |first1=Aaron |title=Five Best Arsenal vs. Chelsea Clashes in Premier League History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1897976-five-best-arsenal-vs-chelsea-clashes-in-premier-league-history |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=23 October 2020 |date=22 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Steen |first1=Sam |title=Five best ever games between Chelsea and Arsenal |url=https://thefootballfaithful.com/best-chelsea-arsenal-games/ |website=thefootballfaithful.com |access-date=23 October 2020 |date=31 July 2020}}</ref>

[[File:Chelsea vs. Arsenal, 29 May 2019 13.jpg|thumb|In May 2019, the two teams contested the [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|UEFA Europa League final]].]]
On 22 March 2014, in [[Arsène Wenger]]'s 1,000th game in charge, Chelsea won 6–0. This marked the most goals Chelsea had scored against Arsenal, Chelsea's biggest margin of victory against Arsenal and the joint heaviest margin of defeat suffered by Wenger at Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lewis |first1=Aimee |title=Chelsea 6–0 Arsenal|website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/26590673 |access-date=30 May 2019 |date=22 March 2014}}</ref> Notable incidents in the match included Chelsea jumping out to a three-goal lead inside of 15 minutes, as well as the sending off of [[Kieran Gibbs]] by referee [[Andre Marriner]] for a handball committed by his teammate [[Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Referee Andre Marriner apologises for Kieran Gibbs red card error |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/26699009 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=29 December 2019 |date=23 March 2014}}</ref>

On 5 October 2014, Chelsea beat Arsenal 2–0, which meant Arsenal manager Wenger had not won against [[José Mourinho]] in twelve attempts. This game also featured former Arsenal captain Cesc Fàbregas playing against his former club for Chelsea for the first time, recording an assist on [[Diego Costa]]'s goal. The match, however, is most notable for a touchline fracas that occurred between the managers in the technical area during the fierce match.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Chelsea 2–0 Arsenal|website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/29398780 |access-date=30 May 2019 |date=5 October 2014}}</ref> On 2 August 2015, Wenger finally recorded a win against Mourinho, defeating Chelsea 1–0 in the [[2015 FA Community Shield]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/33667216 |title= Arsenal 1–0 Chelsea |website=BBC Sport|location=UK | last= Cryer |first=Andy | date=2 August 2015 | access-date=4 August 2015}}</ref>

On 24 September 2016, Arsenal beat Chelsea 3–0 at the Emirates Stadium. It was the first time Arsenal scored against Chelsea since 2013, and Arsenal's first win over The Blues since 2011 in the Premier League. All three goals were scored in the first half by [[Alexis Sánchez]], [[Theo Walcott]] and [[Mesut Özil]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.teamtalk.com/news/vintage-arsenal-a-joy-to-watch-contes-defensive-crisis|title= Vintage Arsenal a joy to watch; Conte's defensive crisis |work=teamtalk.com | date=24 September 2016 | access-date=24 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/sep/24/arsenal-chelsea-premier-league-live|date=24 September 2016|title=Arsenal 3–0 Chelsea|website=The Guardian}}</ref> It was Arsenal's biggest win over Chelsea since 1997.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/news/sports/1094109/wenger-hails-arsenal-after-win-over-chelsea |title= Wenger hails Arsenal after win over Chelsea |work=Bangkok Post |location=Thailand | date=24 September 2016 | access-date=24 September 2016}}</ref>

The two teams have met in the [[2017 FA Cup final]], where Arsenal won their record 13th FA Cup trophy by defeating Chelsea 2–1.<ref name="2017FA">{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39984089|title=Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea|date=27 May 2017|website=BBC Sport|access-date=27 May 2017}}</ref> Arsenal repeated the feat in the [[2017 FA Community Shield]], winning 4–1 on penalties after the match ended 1–1. It was also the first time the "ABBA" penalty taking system has been used by [[The Football Association]].<ref name="2017CS">{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/40766983|title=Arsenal 1–1 Chelsea|date=6 August 2017|website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> On 29 May 2019, the two teams met in their first-ever European final, doing so in the [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|Europa League]], where Chelsea defeated Arsenal 4–1 to clinch their second title in the competition.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bevan |first1=Chris |title=Chelsea beat Arsenal 4–1 to win Europa League final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48368406 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=30 May 2019 |date=29 May 2019}}</ref> The game was also the final career match of [[Petr Čech]], who played for both teams between 2004 and 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Walker-Roberts |first1=James |title=Chelsea 4–1 Arsenal: Eden Hazard scores twice in Europa League final |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-arsenal/report/407117 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=30 May 2019 |date=29 May 2019}}</ref> The next season, Arsenal and Chelsea contested in another FA Cup final, which ended in a [[2020 FA Cup final|2–1 victory]] for Arsenal with two goals by [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]], securing their 14th title.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1 August 2020|title=FA Cup final 2020: Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea – Aubameyang double secures victory|website=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53546100|access-date=2 August 2020}}</ref>

In the [[2020–21 Premier League]], Arsenal completed their first Premier League "double" over Chelsea since 2003–04 after winning both games of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0–1 Arsenal: Blues boss Thomas Tuchel accepts responsibility for loss |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56990160 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=24 July 2021 |date=12 May 2021|first=Gary|last=Rose}}</ref>

==Players who have played for or managed both teams==
Despite being rivals on the pitch, both Arsenal and Chelsea have maintained pragmatic [[business relations]] off it with frequent player transfers, including direct moves between the two clubs. This pattern of exchange reflects a mutual willingness to engage in high-level negotiations despite competitive tensions. By contrast, dealings involving [[Tottenham Hotspur]] are rare as both clubs have generally avoided conducting major transfer business with them. As of the [[2025–26 in English football|2025–26 season]], at least 13 direct transfers have taken place between Arsenal and Chelsea since the start of the [[Premier League]] era, highlighting the unusual nature of their transactional openness for a rivalry in contrast to other club rivalries in England.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cormack |first1=James |title=Every Player to Join Arsenal From Chelsea and How They Fared |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/every-player-join-arsenal-from-chelsea-how-they-fared |website=SI |access-date=19 July 2025 |date=11 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Pearson |first1=Nicola |title=The transfer trend between Arsenal and Chelsea - send us your thoughts |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/transfer-trend-between-arsenal-chelsea-162643259.html |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=19 July 2025 |date=18 July 2025}}</ref>

Below are the players and managers who played for or managed both clubs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.90min.com/posts/2563133-chelsea-vs-arsenal-10-players-who-played-for-both-sides|title=Chelsea vs Arsenal: 10 Players Who Played for Both Sides|website=90min.com|access-date=26 May 2017|archive-date=23 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923012424/http://www.90min.com/posts/2563133-chelsea-vs-arsenal-10-players-who-played-for-both-sides|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/9/english-football/2010/10/01/2145356/from-ashley-cole-to-george-graham-the-footballers-who-have|title=From Ashley Cole To George Graham – The Footballers Who Have Played For Both Chelsea And Arsenal|website=Goal.com|last=Lister|first=Graham}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Willian the latest to cross Chelsea-Arsenal divide - will Brazilian be a success? |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12040/12042851/willian-the-latest-to-cross-chelsea-arsenal-divide-will-brazilian-be-a-success |website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 October 2020 |date=14 August 2020}}</ref>

* Arsenal 1–2 Chelsea: 88,103 (18 April 2009), Wembley (neutral)<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 18 April 2009 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/arsenal-v-chelsea-18-april-2009-284947/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref>
* Arsenal 1–0 Chelsea: 85,437 (2 August 2015), Wembley (neutral)<ref name="2016CS">{{cite web|url=http://www.11v11.com/matches/arsenal-v-chelsea-02-august-2015-317287/|title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 02 August 2015|website=11v11.com|access-date=9 February 2017}}</ref>
* Arsenal 1–1 Chelsea: 83,325 (6 August 2017), Wembley (neutral)<ref name="2017CS1">{{cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/arsenal-v-chelsea-06-august-2017-354413/|title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 06 August 2017|website=11v11.com|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref>
* Chelsea 1–1 Arsenal: 82,905 (12 October 1935), [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] (Chelsea home)<ref name="attendances"/>
* Arsenal 2–0 Chelsea: 73,963 (4 May 2002), [[Millennium Stadium]] (neutral)<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 04 May 2002 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/arsenal-v-chelsea-04-may-2002-12273/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref>
* Arsenal 1–2 Chelsea: 70,073 (25 February 2007), Millennium Stadium (neutral)<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 25 February 2007 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/arsenal-v-chelsea-25-february-2007-277079/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=5 February 2021}}</ref>
* Arsenal 1–1 Chelsea: 68,084 (5 April 1952), [[White Hart Lane]] (neutral)<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 05 April 1952 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/arsenal-v-chelsea-05-april-1952-210213/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref>
* Chelsea 2–1 Woolwich Arsenal: 65,000 (9 November 1907), Stamford Bridge (Chelsea home)<ref name="1stmatch"/>
* Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea: 62,746 (20 March 1973), [[Arsenal Stadium|Highbury]] (Arsenal home)<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 20 March 1973 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/arsenal-v-chelsea-20-march-1973-213508/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref>
